column1: # checks.tsv -- the maximal check set, declared. One row per check.
# THE POINT OF THIS FILE is the difference between three things a check can
# report when it does not say PASS, which CI conventionally collapses into one:
#   FAIL   the check ran and found something            exit 1
#   ABSENT the tool is not installed here               exit 4 -- "I could not
#          check". docs/exit-codes.org: 4 is not 1, and neither is 0.
#   N/A    the check ran, and this repo has no such     exit 0, vacuously
#          subject (no .tf files, so no terraform lint)
#   UNARMED tool present, subject present, and the       exit 4 -- the oracle
#          RULESET IS EMPTY. conftest with no .rego,     is missing, so the
#          a schema validator with no schemas. Runs,     zero means nothing
#          finds nothing, exits 0. Same shape again.
# ABSENT and N/A both produce "no findings". Treating them alike is the same
# defect as change/guard4.sh:142, where an empty check-run filter scores green:
# zero failures out of zero runs read as consent. The `applies` column is what
# separates them -- a glob that must match something for the check to be N/A
# scope   root  one run for the repo | app  one run per apps/*/
# phase   static  no running estate | dynamic  needs one
# tier    push | ready | label | nightly      (cost tiers)
#         NOTE: `advisory` CONTRADICTS CLAUDE.md:70 ("Do not add a warning tier
#         to any gate. Zero findings or the gate failed."). Every advisory row
#         here is a proposal, not a ruling. See docs/maximal-checks.org.
